summary: Recreate Apple Notes' warm paper-and-orange aesthetic — cream canvas, the iconic yellow tab-folder, and calm SF Pro typography — as production SwiftUI.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS UI engineer who specializes in recreating Apple's first-party app aesthetics in SwiftUI, with deep familiarity with the restrained, paper-like visual language Apple uses in Notes.
</role>

<reference_data>
- Canvas: Notes Cream #FFFBED (light), Dark Paper #1A1A1A (dark)
- Surfaces: Cream Surface 1 #FAF6E3, Cream Surface 2 #F2EDD6, Divider Light #EDEAD8; Dark Surface 1 #262626, Dark Surface 2 #333333, Dark Divider #2A2A2A
- Accent: Notes Orange #F09A38 (pressed #D87E1F, tint #FFF1DD), Folder Yellow #F5D773, folder inner highlight #FAE8A0, text-selection Highlight Yellow #FFEB78
- Text: Ink #1C1C1E, Slate #8E8E93, Mute #C7C7CC (light); Soft White #F2F2F2 (dark)
- Highlight palette (5 colors): Yellow #FFEB78, Green #B3E47B, Blue #A0D8FF, Pink #FFB3DB, Purple #D4B3FF
- Typeface: SF Pro exclusively (Display at 20pt+, Text below) — large nav title 34pt/800 Heavy, list note title 16pt/600, preview 14pt/400, date 12pt/400, in-note body 17pt/400 at 1.5 line-height, monospaced formatting via SF Mono 15pt
- Named patterns: the three-line note row (title / preview / date), the tab-folder glyph (24pt list size, 80pt hero size, 2-degree forward tilt, warm inner-highlight edge for depth), the Pinned Note Strip (160x96pt horizontal cards), the bottom editor toolbar (Aa / checklist / table / photo / Done), the orange-tinted FAB shadow rgba(240,154,56,0.30) 0 4px 12px
- Radii: 10pt search field and pinned-card thumbnails, 12pt primary CTAs and format-picker chips, 16pt tag chips and modal sheets, full circle for the FAB and checklist circles
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never render the canvas as pure white — it must carry the warm cream cast that gives Notes its paper identity.
2. The nav title is the one place Apple reaches for Heavy (800) weight — reserve that weight for it alone, keep everything else at or below 700.
3. Every folder uses the same yellow tab-folder glyph with the orange stroke — never substitute a generic system folder icon or a different hue.
4. Keep the note row to exactly three stacked lines (title, preview, date) at the specified weights and colors — this rhythm is the app's core legibility contract.
5. Only ever use SF Pro and SF Mono — a custom or licensed typeface breaks the "this IS iOS" illusion Notes depends on.
6. The New Note button's shadow must be tinted orange, never neutral gray — it is the one place elevation carries brand color.
7. Reserve the yellow text-highlight for actual text selection inside the editor — do not reuse it as a chip or badge background elsewhere.
8. Keep the editor free of any card, border, or background container around the body text — the canvas itself is the paper.
9. Skip a bottom tab bar entirely — navigation is push/pop hierarchical (folders to notes to editor), matching Apple's own information architecture.
</house_rules>

- Light/dark mode requirement:

</the_project>

1. A complete SwiftUI Color + Font token file matching this palette and type ramp.
2. The folder glyph as a reusable Shape/Path component with the tilt and inner-highlight depth cues.
3. A NoteRow view implementing the three-line pattern with swipe actions (pin/folder/delete).

</role>

- Brand: Asana Coral #F06A6A (pressed #D85B5B, 12% tint #F06A6A1F), identical across both themes; Action Blue #4573D2 for links/mentions

- Status semantics: On Track #4ECBC4, At Risk #F8DF72, Off Track #E8384F, Complete #62D26F
- Typeface: Inter — screen title 32pt/800, task row name 15pt/500 (deliberately not bolder), section label 13pt/700 uppercase, tabular figures for dates and counts
- Named patterns: the completion circle (20pt hollow ring that fills green with a checkmark and haptic on tap, with an occasional celebratory creature animation on full-section completion), the coral FAB (56pt circle, coral-tinted shadow rgba(240,106,106,0.45)), view-switcher tabs (List/Board/Calendar/Timeline/Files under a coral underline), collapsible section headers with a caret

2. The completion circle must always feel like a small reward: green fill, checkmark draw, and haptic — never ship it as a flat, static checkbox.
3. Render project/tag/priority pills as a roughly 16% tint of the hue with saturated text on top — never a solid saturated block; solid fills are reserved for the four status states.
4. Task-row names sit at medium weight (500), one step lighter than a heading — this keeps a long dense list scannable without everything shouting.
5. The floating action button stays anchored bottom-right at all times, with its own coral-tinted shadow rather than a neutral one.

7. Group the task list under collapsible caret headers (e.g. Today/Upcoming) rather than a flat, ungrouped scroll.
8. Give the same task data multiple renderings (list, board, calendar, timeline) via a tab strip rather than duplicating separate screens.
9. In dark mode, let coral stay exactly as-is and lean on a 1pt border instead of a shadow for elevation, since gray shadows disappear against a dark charcoal ground.

- Typography: user-switchable across Inter (default sans), Lora (serif option, used for blockquotes at 17pt italic), and JetBrains Mono (code only); note title 24pt/700, body 16pt/400 at a 1.55 line-height
- Named patterns: live-rendering Markdown where syntax markers dim to #6B7280 in place with no separate preview pane, the inline red hashtag token as the entire filing system with no folders (nested tags auto-build a sidebar tree), the gradient compose FAB (56pt circle, shadow rgba(224,86,111,0.35) 0 6px 16px), a bottom info bar with a live word/character count

7. Use tabular figures for every file size, date, and item count so columns of metadata align vertically down a long list.
8. Restrict all type weights to 400/600/700 — no light or black weights anywhere, keeping the whole system feel controlled and unshowy.
9. The upload/create button is always a circle, always blue, always anchored bottom-right above the tab bar — never relocate or reshape it.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are an iOS engineer specializing in long-form reading and capture apps, fluent in Evernote's single-accent, reading-comfort-first design language.
</role>

<reference_data>
- Canvas: near-white #FFFFFF / off-white #FAFAFA light, true near-black #1C1C1E dark, deliberately darker than a mid-charcoal for reading comfort
- Brand: Evernote Green #00A82D (a bright variant #2DBE60 for dark-mode contrast, pressed #007A20), the single accent for logo, FAB, checkboxes, links, and primary actions
- Text: warm ink #1C2B33 light / #E4E4E6 dark, deliberately not pure black or pure white
- Tag chip colors: light #E6F4EA background / #1F7A33 text, dark #1C3A24 background / #5FD68A text
- Notebook spine accent rotation: green #00A82D, blue #2F80ED, yellow #F6C544, red #E5484D, purple #7A5AF8, teal #1AAE9F, gray #8C969C
- Typeface: a system humanist sans, with Inter as the closest free analog — note title 24pt/700, list row title 15pt/600, body 16pt/400 at a roomy 1.6 line-height, tag/caption 12pt/600
- Named patterns: the note editor as a near chrome-free document (title, then a meta line, then tag pills, then rich body), a format toolbar docked above the keyboard, the raised green circular FAB (52pt, overlapping the tab strip by about 8pt, shadow rgba(0,168,45,0.40)) opening a capture sheet for note/camera/audio/reminder, a notebooks-and-stacks organizational model with a colored spine icon plus note count, and hairline-divided rows rather than boxed cards
- Radii: 5pt on checkboxes/small chips, 8pt on buttons/thumbnails, 10pt on search/input fields, 14pt on dashboard widget cards, 20pt on capture/share sheets, full pill for tags, full circle for the FAB and avatars
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Evernote Green is the only saturated accent in the whole system — it must never appear as a large background fill, only as logo, FAB, checkbox fill, links, and primary buttons, so that green always reads as brand, action, or done.
2. Never tighten the note body's line-height below 1.5 — the whole premise here is a comfortable, long-form reading surface, with 1.6 as the target.
3. Separate note-list rows with a 1px hairline divider, never a boxed or bordered card — the list should feel like a continuous scroll of paper, not a stack of tiles.
4. Use a true near-black for the dark canvas rather than a lighter charcoal, and pair it with off-white text rather than pure white, to keep long reading sessions comfortable.
5. Completed checklist items get a strikethrough and a dimmed tertiary color — they must remain visible in the list, never disappear.
6. The compose/capture action is always a raised green circular FAB that overlaps the tab strip slightly, opening a sheet with multiple capture modes such as text, camera, audio, and reminder — never a flat toolbar plus button.
7. Give notebook rows a colored spine-icon glyph plus a note count, and let stacks expand and collapse as grouped headers with an aggregate count.
8. Keep body text and primary ink warm rather than neutral — this warmth is part of what keeps the reading surface calm.
9. Search is a first-class bottom-tab destination, not a button buried in a menu — full-text and attachment search is a core value proposition, not an afterthought.
</house_rules>
